TECH3_2021-1.exp: This is the textbook PMBOK example for 'Market demand' as a project-initiation driver: a car company building fuel-efficient cars because of gasoline shortages is responding to demand in the marketplace, not an internal business need.

TECH3_2021-2.exp: PMBOK's Project Manager Competency Development (PMCD) framework groups PM competencies into three categories: Knowledge, Performance, and Personal competence.

TECH3_2021-3.exp: Writing the detailed scope statement for a specific project and its product is the individual project manager's job, not the PMO's; the PMO instead handles coaching/oversight, shared resources, and organization-wide policy per PMBOK.

TECH3_2021-4.exp: Project resources broadly cover manpower, machinery, and materials together, so 'all of the above' is correct.

TECH3_2021-5.exp: PMBOK defines a 'process' as a set of interrelated actions performed in a sequence to achieve a specified result within the project, which matches 'networked activities aimed at project goals' better than 'project' itself does.

TECH3_2021-6.exp: PMBOK's list of organizational process/procedure assets includes financial control procedures, risk control procedures, and closure guidelines explicitly; 'guidelines of the project to specify needs of the organization' is not part of that standard list and reads as the odd option out.

TECH3_2021-7.exp: The project life cycle spans understanding scope, setting objectives, and formulating/planning activities, so all three together describe it.

TECH3_2021-8.exp: A generic product/project development flow runs Marketing (identify need) -> Analysis and evaluation -> Design -> Inspection, testing and delivery, i.e. ii, iii, i, iv.

TECH3_2021-9.exp: Per PMBOK, dedicated teams are typical of projectized organizations and part-time teams of functional ones, while matrix organizations mainly produce 'mixed' (part dedicated, part part-time) teams rather than uniformly using both types as a defining feature; the other three statements are directly supported by PMBOK's team-composition discussion. The options are close enough that this is a judgment call.

TECH3_2021-10.exp: PMBOK treats the project life cycle as independent of the product life cycle -- a product's life cycle can span many projects across its life, so the two are not the same thing nor strictly interdependent.

TECH3_2021-11.exp: In the PMBOK process-group diagram, Initiating finishes before Closing begins, so those two do not overlap in time, whereas Planning/Executing/Monitoring-Controlling all overlap with each other and with Closing at the tail end.

TECH3_2021-12.exp: The standard PMBOK process group sequence is Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, Closing.

TECH3_2021-13.exp: The bulk of project spend goes into producing deliverables, which happens in the Executing Process Group.

TECH3_2021-14.exp: 'Interchangeable staff' is not a recognized success factor in project management literature (and undermines accountability/expertise); competent team members, client responsiveness, and control mechanisms are standard success factors.

TECH3_2021-15.exp: PMBOK's description of the Closing Process Group explicitly includes applying appropriate updates to organizational process assets as part of formally completing the project or phase.

TECH3_2021-16.exp: A Scope Statement is a project document/output, not an Enterprise Environmental Factor; organizational infrastructure, government standards, and marketplace conditions are all classic EEFs feeding Develop Project Charter.

TECH3_2021-17.exp: Bringing in an outside consultant to advise on developing the Project Charter is the PMBOK tool/technique 'Expert Judgment'; the other options are not standard PMBOK terms.

TECH3_2021-18.exp: Raw, unprocessed measurements like technical performance figures, activity start/finish dates, change request counts, and defect counts are exactly PMBOK's definition of Work Performance Data, before they are analyzed into information or reports.

TECH3_2021-19.exp: The Project Charter is a sponsor-authorized founding document that is not normally revised through routine change requests the way the project management plan and other project documents are, unlike the recognized change-request categories (defect repair/update, corrective/preventive action) and the fact that requests can originate internally or externally, which are all textbook-accurate. This one is a closer call than the others.

TECH3_2021-20.exp: PMBOK defines the Change Control Board (CCB) as the formally chartered group responsible for reviewing, evaluating, and approving or rejecting changes; 'Change Configuration Board' and 'Configuration Control Board' are not the PMBOK term even though both abbreviate to CCB.
